title: Scraper bug: Gigabyte server returns 0 boards silently
description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

The Gigabyte server scraper (CL-83) runs to completion without raising any
exceptions, but `list_boards()` returns an empty list, so `psp-etl scrape
gigabyte-server` produces 0 ROMs and 0 errors — silent failure.

## Likely root cause

Gigabyte's enterprise catalog at
https://www.gigabyte.com/Enterprise/Server-Motherboard?fid=2816 is fronted by
Akamai (same WAF as the consumer www.gigabyte.com). The scraper's parser likely
runs against an Akamai bot-challenge HTML page that doesn't contain product
cards, so the BeautifulSoup extraction finds 0 entries and quietly returns [].

## Fix

1. Add a sanity assertion in `list_boards()` that fails loudly if the parsed
   page has 0 product cards AND no recognizable Akamai challenge marker — at
   least we'll know detection is broken vs. catalog truly empty.
2. Reuse the consumer Gigabyte scraper's _HEADERS dict end-to-end (the CL-83
   commit reuses Akamai-bypassing client plumbing but may not propagate
   *every* sec-ch-ua header to enterprise.* requests).
3. If still blocked: fall back to Wayback CDX against
   `gigabyte.com/Enterprise/Server-Motherboard/MZ*-rev-*/support` (per-board
   pages get archived).

## Acceptance criteria

- `uv run psp-etl scrape gigabyte-server --dry-run` lists at least 5 MZ-prefix
  boards (MZ31-AR0, MZ32-AR0, MZ33-AR0, MZ72-HB0, MZ73-LM0 are known to exist
  on the catalog)
- silent empty-board-list failure is no longer possible

Refs: CL-83.
